import os, glob, torch, torch_npu, time
import torch.nn.functional as F
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from transformers.models.qwen3_5.modeling_qwen3_5 import Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration, Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet, l2norm
DEV="npu:0"
snap = glob.glob(os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--Qwen--Qwen3.5-0.8B/snapshots/*"))[0]
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(snap)
model = Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(snap, dtype=torch.float32).eval().to(DEV)
old = torch.load("gdn_tensors.pt", weights_only=False)
texts = old["samples"]; toks = old["tokens"]

store={}; cur={"n":None}
layers=[m for m in model.modules() if isinstance(m, Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet)]
def wrap(layer):
    orig = layer.chunk_gated_delta_rule
    def f(q,k,v,g,beta,**kw):
        d = store[cur["n"]].setdefault(layer.layer_idx,{})
        d["k"] = l2norm(k[0].float(), dim=-1, eps=1e-6).half().cpu()   # [T,H,128] exactly what kernel uses
        d["q"] = l2norm(q[0].float(), dim=-1, eps=1e-6).half().cpu()
        d["v"] = v[0].float().half().cpu()
        d["beta"] = beta[0].float().cpu(); d["g"] = g[0].float().cpu()
        return orig(q,k,v,g,beta,**kw)
    layer.chunk_gated_delta_rule = f
for l in layers: wrap(l)

with torch.no_grad():
    for n in texts:
        ids = toks[n].unsqueeze(0).to(DEV)
        cur["n"]=n; store[n]={}
        t=time.time(); model(input_ids=ids, use_cache=False)
        print(n, ids.shape[1], f"{time.time()-t:.1f}s", flush=True)
torch.save({"store":store,"tokens":toks,"samples":texts}, "gdn_keys.pt")
print("saved")
provenance.source_readme:
# Qwen3.5 GDN: distributions of the log gate `g` and the write strength `beta`

Measured on `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` (fp32) over 6 prompts (3 prose, 3 code), 346-1024 tokens each.
18 linear-attention layers x 16 value heads = **1,404,288 token-head samples**.
Tensors captured at the call site of `chunk_gated_delta_rule`, so these are exactly the kernel inputs.

## Definitions

```python
b     = in_proj_b(h)                              # [T, 16]  raw logit
beta  = b.sigmoid()                               # write strength, in (0,1)

a     = in_proj_a(h)                              # [T, 16]  raw logit
g     = -A_log.float().exp() * softplus(a + dt_bias)   # log-decay, <= 0   <-- kernel input
alpha = g.exp()                                   # per-step retention, in (0,1]
```

`A = exp(A_log)` and `dt_bias` are per-head learned scalars (16 each).
The kernel receives `g`, never `alpha`. `alpha` is the interpretable scale.

## Global percentiles

| | p0 | p1 | p5 | p25 | p50 | p75 | p95 | p99 | p100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `b` raw | -27.46 | -5.97 | -4.24 | -1.97 | -0.61 | 0.61 | 2.43 | 3.90 | 11.69 |
| **`beta`** | 1.2e-12 | 0.003 | 0.014 | 0.123 | **0.353** | 0.649 | 0.919 | 0.980 | <1 |
| `a` raw | -19.17 | -7.98 | -6.12 | -3.58 | -1.91 | -0.42 | 1.54 | 3.03 | 13.91 |
| **`g`** | -9.315 | -3.134 | -1.547 | -0.140 | **-0.006** | ~0 | ~0 | ~0 | ~0 |
| **`alpha`** | 9.0e-5 | 0.044 | 0.213 | 0.869 | **0.994** | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |

**The two are shaped completely differently.**
`beta` is broad and near-uniform; `alpha` is pinned against 1.

## `beta`: broad, mildly zero-skewed

| | fraction |
|---|---|
| `beta` in (0.1, 0.9) | **72.0%** |
| `beta` < 0.01 | 3.73% |
| `beta` > 0.99 | 0.50% |

Histogram is close to flat: every 0.05-wide bin above 0.1 holds 3-7% of mass,
with a single pile-up in `[0, 0.05)` at 13.3%.
Treat it as a genuine continuous control, not a switch.

## `g` / `alpha`: saturated at no-forgetting

| | fraction |
|---|---|
| `alpha` > 0.9 | 72.6% |
| `alpha` > 0.99 | **53.6%** |
| `alpha` > 0.999 | 37.0% |
| `alpha` > 0.9999 | 19.4% |
| `alpha` < 0.5 | 11.5% |
| `alpha` < 0.01 | 0.18% |

`g` histogram (fraction of all samples):

| range | frac | | range | frac |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `[-0.001, 0)`    | **0.370** | | `[-0.1, -0.05)` | 0.059 |
| `[-0.01, -0.001)`| **0.166** | | `[-0.2, -0.1)`  | 0.059 |
| `[-0.02, -0.01)` | 0.053 | | `[-0.5, -0.2)`  | 0.078 |
| `[-0.05, -0.02)` | 0.073 | | `[-1, -0.5)`    | 0.058 |
| | | | `[-2, -1)`      | 0.051 |
| | | | `[-5, -2)`      | 0.032 |
| | | | `[-10, -5)`     | 0.001 |

**37% of all `g` values lie in `[-0.001, 0)`.** This is the numerics-critical fact: the
bulk of the distribution sits where bf16 spacing is ~4e-6, so representable `g` values
map to retention factors differing by only a few ppm. Keep `g` and the `cumsum(g)` in fp32.
The reference implementation casts to float before computing `g` for exactly this reason.

## Extremes

| | value |
|---|---|
| min `beta` | 1.18e-12 (sigmoid underflow of `b = -27.5`) |
| max `beta` | <1 (never exactly 1.0 in fp32) |
| min `alpha` | **9.0e-5** (`g = -9.315`) |
| `alpha == 1.0` exactly in fp32 | 0.27% of samples |
| `g == 0.0` exactly | never |

Tail mass below threshold:

| thr | P(`beta` < thr) | P(`alpha` < thr) |
|---|---|---|
| 1e-1 | 2.17e-1 | 2.49e-2 |
| 1e-2 | 3.73e-2 | 1.84e-3 |
| 1e-3 | 3.35e-3 | 2.93e-4 |
| 1e-4 | 1.80e-4 | 9.26e-6 |
| 1e-5 | 1.28e-5 | 0 |
| 1e-8 | 8.5e-6 | 0 |

`alpha` has a hard floor near 1e-4; `beta` keeps going down to 1e-12.
`beta` denormals do not occur, but `beta` spans 12 decades while `alpha` spans 4.

### Joint corners

| corner | fraction | count |
|---|---|---|
| `beta`<0.01 & `alpha`>0.99 (pure pass-through) | 3.73e-2 | 52,424 |
| `beta`>0.9 & `alpha`<0.1 (hard overwrite) | 5.68e-3 | 7,969 |
| `beta`>0.99 & `alpha`<0.01 (full reset) | 4.77e-5 | 67 |
| `beta`<0.01 & `alpha`<0.01 (erase, write nothing) | 1.42e-6 | 2 |

The "full reset" corner is rare but present. The "erase and write nothing" corner is
essentially absent, so a state that decays to zero without a replacement write is not
a regime the model actually uses.

- **Early layers (0-2) forget hard.** Layer 1 drops below `alpha`=0.5 on 42% of samples.
- **Middle layers (9, 12) barely forget and barely write.** Near-pure accumulation.
- **Late layers (18-22) partially return to forgetting.**
- `beta` traces a U with depth: ~0.5 at both ends, ~0.21 at layer 12.

Hard-forget events (`alpha` < 0.01) are almost entirely a layer-0/1/2 phenomenon:
1940 / 565 / 67 occurrences, versus **zero** in layers 6 through 21.
Within layer 0, 88% of them come from a single head (h0).

## Head structure

Heads specialize sharply and identically across all 6 prompts.
Within one layer, median `alpha` spans the full range:

```
L0  median alpha per head:
[0.025 1.000 1.000 0.034 0.845 1.000 1.000 0.991
 1.000 0.997 1.000 0.071 1.000 0.276 1.000 0.999]

L22 median alpha per head:
[0.991 0.879 0.092 1.000 0.656 1.000 0.998 0.832
 0.987 0.100 0.999 0.248 0.996 1.000 0.997 1.000]
```

Most layers hold a few fast-decay heads beside a majority of near-lossless ones.
Median `beta` per head similarly spans 0.013 to 0.99.
**Per-layer scalar summaries average over heads that behave oppositely** - if your kernel
branches per head, sweep per head.

Underlying cause: `A = exp(A_log)` has layer medians of 0.18-0.54 but outlier heads at
5.4-10.6 (layers 1, 5, 10, 14), and `dt_bias` is mostly negative (layer medians -4.7 to +0.9),
which pushes `softplus(a + dt_bias)` toward 0 and saturates `alpha` at 1.

## Position and content effects

Position 0 is distinct: median `alpha` ~0.73 and median `beta` ~0.95 (strong write into an
empty state). By position 8 it settles to the steady-state profile and stays there.

**Prose vs code is a null result.** Mean `beta` 0.400 vs 0.398, mean `alpha` 0.863 vs 0.865,
P(`alpha`<0.5) 0.117 vs 0.113. All percentiles agree to two decimals. Variation lives in
layer and head identity, not input domain.

## Sampling for tests

```python
beta = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(B,T,H)*2.1 - 0.6)      # med 0.35, P(0.1<b<0.9)=0.72
g    = -0.5*F.softplus(torch.randn(B,T,H)*3.0 - 2.0)    # med alpha 0.94, P(a<0.5)=0.15
```

Matches the global median of `beta` (0.348 vs 0.353) and the forgetting rate
(P(`alpha`<0.5) 0.147 vs 0.115). It does **not** reproduce the deep `g` tail
(P(`alpha`<0.01) 2e-4 vs 1.8e-3) or per-head specialization. For those, add explicit
cases at `g = -9.3` and `beta` just below 1, or use the captured tensors directly.

## Caveats

- One checkpoint (0.8B), max 1024 tokens. `alpha` saturation near 1 is plausibly
  length-dependent; retention is cheap over a short context.
- 6 prompts. Enough for the aggregate shape, not for rare-event rates below ~1e-5.
